kill_reasons.reason: The exact niche this candidate targets — a radically cheap, simplified ZATCA Phase-2 e-invoicing tool for the smallest merchants, priced 'far below full ERP suites' — is already fully occupied by multiple live, Saudi-localized, ZATCA Phase-2-compliant products priced at or below what a solo founder could sustainably charge. BizzSols (bizzsols.com) sells a full ZATCA Phase-2 compliant product at SAR 49/month that already includes QR codes, digital signatures, automatic XML submission to ZATCA, credit/debit notes, VAT reports, inventory tracking AND bank reconciliation — i.e. more features than the candidate's proposed 6-8 week MVP, at a price a solo founder's own unit-economics analysis (in the dossier) shows is barely profitable once payment-processing fees (4-7% of a 60 SAR charge) are counted. Bridge Bills (52 SAR/mo), Fatoora Cloud (75 SAR/mo, 'zero setup'), and FatooraPlus (99 SAR/mo) fill every price point up to Qoyod's established ~120-207 SAR/mo tier, and Zoho Invoice markets itself as free Saudi VAT e-invoicing software with ZATCA QR/XML generation. This collectively closes the low-price wedge the candidate's differentiation strategy depends on — there is no discovered price point or feature gap left for a solo-built entrant to occupy profitably.

evidence.summary: Live commercial product: 'fully ZATCA Phase 2 compliant invoicing for Saudi businesses... starting at 49 SAR/month' with QR codes, digital signatures, automatic XML submission, inventory, full accounting incl. bank reconciliation.
Bridge Bills priced at 52 SAR/month (promo), another sub-60-SAR ZATCA-compliant competitor already in market (per dossier additional_research).
Zoho Invoice markets itself as free VAT e-invoicing software for Saudi small businesses, with ZATCA QR/XML generation included, per its own Saudi-localized marketing page.
Qoyod (established Saudi brand) already has paying customers at 120-600 SAR/month, confirming a mature, well-distributed local incumbent with brand trust already serves this segment.
